name: Back Defense Protocol
description: A guide to selecting Brian Glick's back-escape lessons by controlling side, hooks, body triangle and strangle-defense stage.
summary: Brian Glick's Only Way Out: Dynamic Back Escapes separates rear-mount escapes by overhook side, underhook side, body triangle and special control situations.
overview: Two exchanges both called back control may require different study sections. Glick's outline separates side-specific escapes from lower-body restrictions and strangle defenses, which makes it useful when a general back-escape lesson does not match the position you keep encountering.

products.title: Only Way Out: Dynamic Back Escapes
products.blurb: Seven volumes distinguish rear-control configurations, escape destinations and strangle-defense stages.
products.best_for: Students who need separate study paths for overhook-side, underhook-side and body-triangle problems.
products.study_focus: Begin with defensive hand fighting in Volume 1 at 24:53, then select Volume 2, 3 or 4 for the configuration you identified.

guide.display_title: Back Defense: Brian Glick's Rear-Mount Study Guide

fits: You need to find the lesson that matches your particular rear-mount configuration.
Your recurring problem involves a trapped arm, body triangle or a strangle attempt during an escape.
consider_alternative_if: Your exchange still begins in turtle without established rear mount: Priit Mihkelson Turtle Defense System has a more direct posture-and-exit outline.

includes: Volume 1 introduces rear mount, defensive hand fighting, trapped-arm situations and four named essential skills.
Volumes 2–4 organize overhook-side, underhook-side and body-triangle escapes; Volume 5 adds crucifix, cross-body ride and standing cases.
Volume 6 distinguishes early, middle and late strangle defenses; Volume 7 supplies an executive summary.
limits: This is a rear-control escape course; mount and side-pin recovery are outside its main organizing sections.
Strangle-defense chapter labels identify stages but do not establish how to recognize or execute a late defense.

start_here.title: Identify the back-control configuration before choosing an escape
start_here.task: Pause a back-control exchange at the moment you would begin an escape. Record the upper-body control separately from the legs: which side can you identify, and are hooks or a body triangle visible? Use Volumes 2–4 to locate the matching section. If an arm is trapped or a strangle is already being attempted, mark that as a separate study problem and locate Volume 1 or 6 rather than assuming the same starting conditions.
start_here.section: Volume 1: Essential Skills - 1 - Gripping - Defensive Hand Fighting Fundamentals (24:53); Volumes 2–4: side-specific and body-triangle escapes
